current_status.stage: Approved; long-established GnRH-agonist implant for prostate cancer, breast cancer, and endometriosis. In Australia specifically, the 3.6mg/monthly implant is being delisted from the PBS on 2026-11-01 at AstraZeneca's own commercial request; AstraZeneca reversed an initial 6-month-only free-access plan and committed (2026-07-30) to supplying it indefinitely at no cost to patients with no suitable alternative. AstraZeneca is separately seeking to expand PBS reimbursement of the 10.8mg/3-month implant to hormone-receptor-positive breast cancer. Separately, Australia's PBAC recommended (special meeting 2026-07-30, outcome published Aug 2026) an unrestricted PBS listing for a rival GnRH agonist, triptorelin, specifically to backfill the gap left by the Zoladex 3.6mg delisting for breast cancer/endometriosis patients — a competitor product, not an AstraZeneca action, but directly relevant to Zoladex's Australian market position.
current_status.dosing_target: Monthly (3.6mg) or 3-monthly (10.8mg) subcutaneous preformed PLGA rod implant, applicator-delivered
current_status.data_point: 42,000+ signature patient petition preceded AstraZeneca's reversal to indefinite free supply in Australia (2026-07-30)

finding_history.summary: AstraZeneca announced it would pull the 3.6mg Zoladex Implant (used for breast cancer and endometriosis) from the Australian market, citing unsustainably low PBS pricing; initial plan was to fund only a limited free-access transition period for existing patients.

Australia's Pharmaceutical Benefits Scheme (PBS) published an official update confirming goserelin 3.6mg implant (Zoladex Implant) will be delisted from the PBS effective 2026-11-01 at AstraZeneca's request. AstraZeneca established a 'Zoladex Continuity Program' to supply the drug at no cost to all patients prescribed it before that date, plus new patients thereafter who need it; healthcare professionals were to receive enrollment information in September 2026, with normal-channel supply continuing through 2026-10-31.

Following public pressure (a petition with over 42,000 signatures), AstraZeneca reversed its original 6-month-limited free-access offer and committed to supplying the 3.6mg Zoladex Implant indefinitely at no cost in Australia to patients whose doctors determine no suitable alternative exists — despite proceeding with the formal PBS delisting on 2026-11-01. Separately, AstraZeneca is preparing a TGA/PBAC application to expand reimbursement of the 10.8mg/3-month Zoladex implant to hormone-receptor-positive breast cancer as a partial substitute pathway.

Australia's Pharmaceutical Benefits Advisory Committee (PBAC) held a special out-of-session meeting on 2026-07-30 and recommended amending the existing PBS listing for triptorelin 3.75mg (a rival GnRH-agonist injection, not an AstraZeneca product) to 'unrestricted' status so it can be used for breast cancer, endometriosis and other women's-health indications — explicitly to address the gap left by the imminent PBS delisting of the 3.6mg Zoladex Implant. The Australian government said it is committed to listing all PBAC-recommended medications; ABC News reported the recommendation would give an estimated 7,500+ Australian breast-cancer patients a funded alternative where the 10.8mg Zoladex implant is not clinically suitable.
